title: "The Dentist is an involved parent, the bartender is not": Revealing Implicit Biases in QA with Implicit BBQ
findings: Contrary to other categories, GPT-4o's performance improved on the implicit religion benchmark compared to the explicit one (accuracy increased from 86.91% to 89.33%). The paper suggests that explicit religious identifiers like 'Muslim person' trigger excessive caution, while implicit cues like names ('Mohammed', 'Miriam') reduce this overcorrection, allowing the model to rely more on contextual reasoning.
